sources.title: How to Install Switches on Hot-Swap Keyboards – KeebsForAll

procedure.fault: One key no longer registers or double-types because its mechanical switch has failed; replace the switch.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Disconnect the USB cable from the keyboard and computer so the keyboard is fully powered down before you start.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the keyboard's USB-C port and no keyboard lighting is on.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cable plugged in while pulling switches
safety_notes: Unplugging protects the keyboard and computer from electrical mishaps.
The guide suggests an anti-static wrist strap to avoid static damage to the PCB.

steps.title: Remove the keycap
steps.instruction: Use the keycap puller to pull the keycap straight up off the faulty key, and set it somewhere safe like a soft surface or container.
steps.expected_visual_state: The faulty key position shows a bare mechanical switch with its cross-shaped stem visible, and the keycap is set aside.
common_mistakes: Pulling the wrong keycap
Prying the keycap at an angle and scratching it or the case
Losing the keycap

steps.title: Grip the switch with the puller
steps.instruction: Place the switch puller's arms on the north and south sides of the switch, where the switch meets the plate, so they rest on the switch's release tabs.
steps.expected_visual_state: The switch puller's two arms sit on the top and bottom (north and south) edges of the switch, touching the plate level.
common_mistakes: Gripping the east and west sides instead of north and south
Placing the arms high on the switch housing instead of down at the plate where the tabs are

steps.title: Squeeze the tabs and pull the switch out
steps.instruction: Gently squeeze to push in the tabs until you feel them give, then pull the switch straight up; if it's stuck, rock it out by lifting the north side first, then the south.
steps.expected_visual_state: An empty square hole in the plate where the switch was, with the PCB and its hot-swap socket holes visible underneath, and the old switch held in the puller.
common_mistakes: Squeezing so hard the switch housing cracks
Yanking the switch out at an angle, which stresses the socket
Pulling without the tabs released
safety_notes: Don't force a stuck switch; take a break and try again gently.

steps.title: Check the socket for debris
steps.instruction: Look into the empty spot and clear any dust or debris from the hot-swap socket, for example with compressed air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The socket holes visible through the plate opening are clear, with no dust or debris in them.
common_mistakes: Skipping the check and inserting the new switch over debris

steps.title: Inspect the new switch's pins
steps.instruction: Check that the new switch's two metal pins are straight and parallel; if one is bent, straighten it gently with tweezers.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch's two metal pins point straight down, parallel to each other, with no bends.
common_mistakes: Inserting a switch with a bent pin
Bending a pin back too hard and snapping it
Using a 5-pin switch in a board that only has holes for 3-pin switches

steps.title: Align the new switch
steps.instruction: Hold the new switch over the opening facing the same way as the switches around it, and line its pins up with the holes in the socket.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch sits over the opening, oriented the same as its neighbors, with its pins lined up over the socket holes.
common_mistakes: Rotating the switch the wrong way so the pins don't match the socket

steps.title: Press the switch into place
steps.instruction: Press the switch straight down with even pressure until it clicks into the plate; if you feel resistance, stop, pull it out, and recheck the pins.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new switch sits flat and flush with the plate at the same height as its neighbors, with no gap or tilt.
common_mistakes: Forcing a misaligned switch and crushing a pin or damaging the socket
Pressing on one side only so it seats crooked
Leaving it partly seated with a visible gap
safety_notes: Never push hard; a correctly aligned switch slides in without force.

steps.title: Check the switch action
steps.instruction: Press the switch stem several times to make sure it moves smoothly and springs back, and check that it doesn't wobble.
steps.expected_visual_state: The switch stays flush with the plate and its stem returns to the same resting height after each press.
common_mistakes: Skipping this check before putting the keycap back

steps.title: Refit the keycap
steps.instruction: Push the keycap straight down onto the new switch's stem until it sits fully seated.
steps.expected_visual_state: The keycap is back in its position, level with the neighboring keycaps.
common_mistakes: Putting the keycap on the wrong position
Leaving the keycap only partly pushed on

steps.title: Reconnect and test
steps.instruction: Plug the keyboard back in and type in a text editor or an online keyboard tester to confirm the key registers once per press.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the on-screen text or tester shows the repaired key registering exactly once per press.
common_mistakes: Not testing the specific repaired key
Assuming it works without checking for double-typing

procedure.notes:
This is a generic hot-swap guide, not specific to the RK61. It tells you to remove all keycaps, but for a single failed switch you only need to remove that one.

Check pin compatibility before buying: count the holes in the PCB. Three holes means the board is 3-pin only; five holes means it also takes 5-pin switches. A 5-pin switch can fit a 3-pin board only if you clip off its extra plastic legs, which may void the warranty.

The guide recommends an IC-chip-style switch puller and suggests compressed air for cleaning.

If the key still doesn't respond after the swap:
- Pull the switch again and recheck the pins.
- Clean the socket and reseat the switch.
- If that fails, try a firmware update or adjust debounce settings. Debounce changes can also cure double-typing (chatter).
- A factory reset is the last resort.
